grid.order: year-major, then row-major from south to north, west to east

caption: NASA AIRS (Aqua satellite) SurfAirTemp · each year 2003–2025 compared with the 2003–2025 average of the same 2° square. A single year is weather as much as climate: the trend map tests the change. Values are stored in steps of 0.0262 °C.

processing: one OPeNDAP DAP4 subset per monthly granule: SurfAirTemp_A, SurfAirTemp_D, TotH2OVap_A, TotH2OVap_D (no other fields)
day/night mean = (ascending ~1:30 pm + descending ~1:30 am) / 2, only where both orbits have a value (37622 native cell-months with a single orbit were left out)
yearly means 2003–2025 in each 2° square minus that square's average over the record
no trend test: a playback of the data behind the trend map
provenance.caveat: Data: NASA AIRS infrared sounder on the Aqua satellite, 1° squares, average of the ~1:30 am and ~1:30 pm passes; a satellite retrieval, not a weather model (MERRA-2 does use AIRS measurements, so the two are not fully independent) (the map averages them into 2° squares). The trend is a straight line through 2003–2025; it shows what changed, not why. The record is 23 years long, shorter than the 30 years usually used to describe a climate. Over hot deserts AIRS and MERRA-2 agree poorly (infrared retrievals over bright desert surfaces are hard), so read desert results with care; elsewhere the two usually agree.
